title: How Dear Is the Thought, That the Angels of God
description: How Dear Is the Thought, That the Angels of God in Tonic Solfa to GORDON, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 355, “Are They Not All Ministering Spirits?”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens (11.11.11.11), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GORDON; any other Elevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: How dear is the thought_, that the an-gels of God May bow their bright wings_ to the world they once trod; Will leave the sweet songs of_ the man_-sions a-bove_, To breathe o'er our bo_-soms some mes_-sage of love!

lines: How dear is the thought, that the angels of God
May bow their bright wings to the world they once trod;
Will leave the sweet songs of the mansions above,
To breathe o'er our bosoms some message of love!
They come, on the wings of the morning they come,
Impatient to lead some poor wanderer home;
Some sinner to save from his darkened abode,
And lay him to rest in the arms of his God.
They come when we wander, they come when we pray,
In mercy to guard us wherever we stray;
A glorious cloud, their bright witness is given;
Encircling us here are these angels of heaven.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to GORDON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
